name: forge-terminal
description: A terminal-native file converter for macOS, Windows and Linux

whatsNew.title: Windows and Linux
whatsNew.text: Transcribe, read text, camera RAW, Boost and remove background now work on Windows and Linux too, as extensions.

whatsNew.title: Read text
whatsNew.text: Transcribe reads the words in pictures and PDFs, including Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Arabic, Hindi and Thai.

whatsNew.title: Transcript formats
whatsNew.text: Save a transcript as Markdown, Word, PDF or plain text.

whatsNew.title: Many files at once
whatsNew.text: Convert, compress and edit take several files or a whole folder. esc stops a batch.

whatsNew.title: Run a preset
whatsNew.text: Run a saved preset from home with p, or from Finder’s Quick Actions. Choose which ones show in /right-click.

whatsNew.title: Camera RAW
whatsNew.text: Photos straight from a camera open like any other picture.

whatsNew.title: More in edit
whatsNew.text: Rotate pictures and video, change a video’s speed, take the sound out of a video, and clean up noisy audio.

whatsNew.title: One way off Done
whatsNew.text: Every Done ends in the same row of buttons: Home, show in Finder, or keep editing.

whatsNew.title: Simpler colour mode
whatsNew.text: Palette is a tab now, More holds the rest, and a gradient can have any number of colours.

whatsNew.title: Your own tools
whatsNew.text: Forge uses the yt-dlp and ffmpeg you already have, and /extensions shows the space each one takes.

author: Atharva Nayak

scripts.lint: biome check src tests scripts extensions
scripts.format: biome format --write src tests scripts extensions
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
